items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: He says, “Son, you’ve got a life of misery ahead of ya.” And I said, “I’m not going to stay on the band that long, Woody.”

ctx.x: That must have been quite an experience. You went overseas?

Yeah. I joined the band in Fort Worth, Texas when I was twenty. I remember it was the day after Christmas and I was absolutely petrified. I flew down there by myself with the bass and joined the band and went to work that night. And it was a great band, Sal Nistico and Bill Chase was on that band, Nat Pierce was playing piano, Ronnie Zito was playing drums. And I went through my growing pains with Woody. I was a kid and very insecure, but I ended up staying — it says in the program I was there for three years,…
Was there a conscious decision at some point, you said I have to move to New York?
